transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I guess what brings me in is, um, I’ve been waking up feeling really heavy and hollow. Sad, mostly. Like… I’m a dancer, and it feels like the studio lights are on but there’s just no music in me anymore. I don’t know if that makes sense.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?

Yeah… I think it did. It was after I hurt my ankle. I mean, I know injuries happen, especially in dance, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that’s when this whole pattern seemed to start. It’s been about two months now, I guess.
Does the sadness feel much stronger than you would expect from being injured?

I mean… I keep telling myself it’s just an ankle, and people deal with worse, so maybe I shouldn’t make too much of it. But yes, it does feel… bigger than that, I think. I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness, like everything’s technically there—the lights, the room—but there’s no music in me. If that makes sense.
Before this started, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this?

Not really like this, no. I mean, I’ve had bad days before—everyone does, I guess—but this waking up with that heavy, hollow sadness… like everything’s there but there’s no music in me… that feels different. I hope that answers what you mean.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in dancing or other things you usually enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I still care about dancing, and I don’t want to sound like I’ve just given up or anything. It’s just… some days it feels harder to feel the same spark. But I don’t know if that’s “lost interest,” exactly. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling anxious a lot lately?
I don’t think so… not a lot, anyway. I mean, I get worried here and there, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. It feels more like I’m just unsettled sometimes. Is that what you mean by anxious?
Have there been things you usually enjoy that just don’t feel pleasurable right now?

I’m not sure… I wouldn’t say things feel completely empty or anything. Maybe some things don’t land the same way right now, but I can’t tell if that’s just being tired or distracted. I still want to enjoy them, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

A little, yes. I mean, not in a terrible way, but I’ve noticed it. Like I’ll sit down to finish something straightforward, like a grant report, and then a truck outside or a photo on the wall or even one phrase in an old rehearsal note will pull me into some totally different idea or plan. I can usually come back to it eventually, but it’s been harder to stay on one thing. Is that what you mean by concentrating?
Have you noticed your appetite has gone down lately?

Maybe a little, yes. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but when I was really buzzing with ideas I’d just forget to eat sometimes, like I’d look up and realize I’d skipped a meal. And now… food is there, but it kind of tastes like cardboard. My rehearsal clothes have been hanging a bit looser, so I guess my appetite has gone down. Is that helpful?
Have you been waking up earlier than usual and not able to fall back asleep?

Yes… I think so. Not every single night, but lately I’ll fall asleep because I’m just exhausted, and then I’m up around four or five with my stomach all tight, and I can’t really settle back down.

Before that there were a few nights where I stayed up way too late sketching formations, almost until dawn, but I told myself that was just work energy. I don’t know if that counts as sleep being “disturbed,” but it’s been kind of all over the place.
During those times when you were buzzing with ideas, did you feel unusually energized or high compared with your normal self?

Yes… I think “unusually energized” is fair. I don’t want to overstate it, but there were stretches where I felt kind of dazzlingly alive, like every idea had light around it and I could see the whole piece coming together.

And then, um… not as flattering, but I’d get really sharp with people if they questioned the plan or reminded me my ankle still needed rest. I’d feel furious suddenly, like they were trying to slow down something important. Does that make sense?
During those energized times, did you feel unusually confident or powerful compared with your normal self?

Yes… though I feel a little embarrassed saying it that way. At the time it didn’t feel like “powerful,” exactly. It felt more like I could turn the whole setback into something meaningful—like a career-defining piece, something that might genuinely change how people think about dance and wilderness.

And I remember being kind of… shocked, honestly, when other people didn’t immediately see what I saw. I thought it was so obvious. Does that answer what you mean?
During those energized times, were you taking on a lot more projects or working much more than usual?

Yes… probably more than usual. I mean, I told myself it was just being productive, trying to make good use of being injured, but I was kind of bouncing from one thing to the next.

I’d be drawing maps, then emailing collaborators, then reorganizing music files, then suddenly trying to redesign the whole project all at once. It felt important at the time, not chaotic exactly… but looking back, it was a lot. Does that make sense?
During those energized times, did they cause serious problems in your life or work?

Yes… I mean, I was still showing up for the essential things, so I don’t want to make it sound like everything completely fell apart.

But, yes, it did cause problems. I fell behind on my teaching prep, and I missed a grant deadline, which is… not like me. And the studio got so disorganized that collaborators started taking over basic scheduling things for me.

I could still function, technically, but not at the level I normally do as a choreographer or teacher. Does that make sense?
About the time when you felt unusually energized and full of ideas, what’s the longest that stretch lasted?

I guess… the longest stretch has really been this whole period since I hurt my ankle. It’s not like one single clear episode with a neat start and stop, but the pattern started after the injury and it’s been going on, in some form, for about two months now.

I know that probably sounds like a long time. I kept thinking it was just me trying to stay useful while I couldn’t dance normally. Does that answer what you’re asking?
During those energized times, were you talking much more than usual?

A little, yes… maybe more than a little, if I’m being honest.

My collaborators mentioned that in meetings I was talking really fast, like they couldn’t quite get a word in. I didn’t mean to steamroll anyone. It just felt like if I paused, the whole idea might disappear before I could explain it.

I know that probably sounds intense. I thought I was just being excited about the work.
During those energized times, were you doing much more than usual?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I wasn’t doing more in a productive, organized way exactly, but I kept moving from one thing to the next.

Even with my ankle, I’d be sitting there drawing out maps for the piece, then emailing collaborators, then reorganizing music files, then suddenly trying to redesign the whole project all at once. It felt important at the time, like I was being useful.

I know that sounds like a lot. I wasn’t trying to be chaotic, but… yes, I was doing much more than usual.
During those energized times, did you feel like you needed less sleep than usual?

Yes… I think so. I mean, my sleep has just been kind of all over the place.

Some nights I’d tell myself I was just going to sketch a few formations, and then suddenly it would be almost dawn. And lately it’s more like I fall asleep because I’m completely exhausted, but then I wake up at four or five with my stomach all tight.

I don’t know if that counts as needing less sleep exactly, but it definitely hasn’t been normal for me.
During the time when you felt unusually energized and needed less sleep, did that elevated feeling last for at least 4 days in a row?

Um… yes, I think it was definitely more than four days.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but this whole pattern really started after my ankle injury, and it’s kind of been going on for about two months now. Not every single day was exactly the same, but the energized, not-sleeping-normal part… it wasn’t just a couple days. Does that make sense?
During those energized times, did you ever hear or see things that other people could not?

Um… I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. It wasn’t like I was seeing people or anything.

But on a few of the really wired days, when I was alone in my apartment, I could hear this kind of low humming voice… almost like wind moving over rock. It felt like it was telling me where the dancers should go, like where they should move next.

I know that probably sounds strange. The windows were closed, so… I don’t really know what to make of it.

I know that probably sounds strange. The windows were closed, so… I don’t really know what to make of it.

inference.note: Auditory perceptual disturbance during an elevated/decreased-sleep period indicates psychotic features in a bipolar mood episode; prior depression plus hypomanic/manic symptoms now most consistent with bipolar affective disorder, current manic episode with psychotic symptoms, ruling out F32.9 and making F31.8 less likely.
